'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Rust shooting incident|''Rust'' shooting incident]]
**[[Cinematographer]] [[Halyna Hutchins]] is killed during the [[Filmmaking#Production|production]] of the upcoming [[American film]] ''[[Rust (2024 film)|Rust]]'' in [[Bonanza City, New Mexico]], while [[film director]] [[Joel Souza]] is in critical condition, after actor [[Alec Baldwin]] reportedly shot a loaded gun. [https://www.straitstimes.com/life/entertainment/alec-baldwin-fired-prop-gun-that-killed-woman-on-film-set-us-police (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Moscow]] [[Mayor of Moscow|mayor]] [[Sergei Sobyanin]] announces a non-working week from October 28 until November 7 in order to reduce the spread of [[COVID-19]]. Only firms that serve essential goods and the city infrastructure would be allowed to operate. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/10/21/moscow-goes-on-partial-lockdown-starting-oct-28-a75363 (''The Moscow Times'')]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 36,339 new cases and 1,030 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|death]]s from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 8.13 million and the nationwide death toll to 227,389. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/russia-hits-new-record-daily-covid-cases-deaths-amid-upward-trend/2398795 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Latvia]]
****[[Latvia]] enters a month-long [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] until November 15 that closes non-essential shops, cinemas and hairdressers, as well as implements a [[curfew]] from 8 p.m. to 5 a.m., due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://medicalxpress.com/news/2021-10-latvia-lockdown-covid-spikes.html (Medical Xpress)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] reports a record 22,415 new cases and 546 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2.7 million and the nationwide death toll to 62,389. [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-health-ukraine-europe-coronavirus-vaccine-5ad7fb543096e0c2278976007ce12860 (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in India]]
****[[India]] reports that it has administered more than one billion [[COVID-19 vaccine|COVID-19 vaccinations]] since it started its [[vaccination]] drive in January. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-56345591 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Saudi Arabia]]
****[[Saudi Arabia]] begins the rollout of [[booster dose]]s of the COVID-19 vaccines for people aged above 18 and have received their second dose at least six months ago. [https://gulfnews.com/amp/world/gulf/saudi/saudi-arabia-allows-covid-19-vaccine-booster-shots-1.83105328 (''Gulf News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
***[[New Zealand]] reports a record 102 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the first the time that the country has reported more than 100 cases since the beginning of the pandemic. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/oct/21/new-zealand-covid-daily-cases-pass-100-for-first-time-since-pandemic-began (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****The [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] announces that the [[United States]] has [[Deployment of COVID-19 vaccines|donated]] 200 million [[COVID-19 vaccine|COVID-19 vaccines]] to countries around the world, fulfilling a pledge from [[President of the United States|president]] [[Joe Biden]] that the U.S. would be the "world's arsenal" in [[vaccine]]s. [https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/577680-white-house-us-has-donated-200-million-covid-19-vaccines-around-the (The Hill)]
****The U.S. [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention]] endorses booster shots of the [[Moderna]] and [[Johnson & Johnson]] vaccines. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/10/21/health/covid-vaccine-boosters-cdc.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 misinformation]]
***[[COVID-19 misinformation by China]]
****The [[University of Oxford]] links the [[Chinese government]] to a [[disinformation]] campaign promoting the [[false accusation|unfounded claim]] that COVID-19 could have been imported to China from the [[United States]] through [[Maine lobster]]s shipped to a seafood market in [[Wuhan]] in November 2019. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/china-linked-disinformation-campaign-blames-covid-maine-lobsters-rcna3236 (NBC News)]
*[[Climate change]]
**[[Greenpeace]] partially leaks a draft report from the [[International Panel on Climate Change]], revealing that a number of large oil, coal, beef and animal feed-producing countries including [[Australia]], [[Saudi Arabia]], [[Brazil]] and [[Argentina]] are lobbying the IPCC for looser restrictions on global heating. [https://apnews.com/article/climate-environment-and-nature-environment-united-nations-greenpeace-308a04052994ecf028ca08c323e10958 (AP)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2021 North Kosovo crisis]]
**A working group to find a more permanent solution to the license plate issue, consisting of negotiators from the governments of [[Kosovo]] and [[Serbia]], meet for the first time in [[Brussels]]. If negotiations are successful, the group will announce their proposals in 6 months. [https://www.gazetatema.net/en/delegations-from-kosovo-and-serbia-meet-to-discuss-a-permanent-solution-to-the-issue-of-license-plates/ (Gazeta Tema)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack]]
**The [[United States House of Representatives]] votes 229–202 to hold former [[Counselor to the President|White House Chief Strategist]] [[Steve Bannon]] in criminal contempt for refusing to comply with a [[subpoena]] issued by the [[January 6th Committee|January 6 select committee]] investigating [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|the attack]] on the [[United States Capitol|U.S. Capitol]]. The contempt is referred to the [[United States Attorney for the District of Columbia|U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia]] and [[United States Attorney General]] [[Merrick Garland]] to decide whether to prosecute Bannon. [https://apnews.com/article/steve-bannon-donald-trump-subpoenas-merrick-garland-house-elections-ea316d27da03c1c2ac467e34fefaf1da (AP)]
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]], [[Vaccine passports during the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**The [[France|French]] [[National Assembly (France)|National Assembly]] votes 135 to 125 to approve the extension of the COVID-19 Health Pass until at least July 31, 2022. The bill will be debated at the [[Senate (France)|French Senate]] on October 28 in preparation for adopting the bill on November 15. [https://www.connexionfrance.com/French-news/French-MPs-back-law-to-keep-possible-use-of-health-pass-until-July-31 (''The Connexion'')] 
*[[Killing of Justine Damond]]
**Former [[Minneapolis Police Department]] officer Mohamed Noor is resentenced to four years and nine months in prison for the [[manslaughter]] of unarmed [[9-1-1]] caller Justine Damond. Noor had originally been [[sentence (law)|sentenced]] to 12.5 years for [[murder]] in 2017. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/10/21/us/mohamed-noor-resentencing/index.html (CNN)]
*Twenty-four people have been [[Capital punishment|executed]] in [[Syria]] for [[Arson|deliberately starting]] [[wildfire]]s in late 2020 that killed three people. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-58997475 (BBC News)]
*The leader of the [[400 Mawozo|Haitian gang]] who kidnapped 17 United States and Canadian [[missionaries]] has threatened to kill the hostages if the gang does not receive the [[United States dollar|$]]17 million [[ransom]] for their release. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/10/21/americas/haiti-missionaries-intl-latam/index.html (CNN)]
*The [[Benin]] [[National Assembly (Benin)|National Assembly]] votes to legalize [[abortion]] within the first three months of pregnancy if it is likely to "aggravate or cause material, educational, professional or moral distress" or is "incompatible with the woman or the unborn child's interest", becoming one of the few countries in [[Africa]] to authorize abortions. [https://www.africanews.com/2021/10/21/west-africa-s-benin-votes-to-legalise-abortion/ (Africanews)] 

'''Politics and elections'''
*''[[Ratu]]'' [[Wiliame Katonivere]] becomes the [[president-elect]] of [[Fiji]]. He will replace incumbent [[President of Fiji|president]] [[Jioji Konrote]] when he is confirmed by [[Parliament of Fiji|parliament]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/453970/ratu-wiliame-katonivere-set-to-be-fiji-s-next-president (RNZ)]
*[[Cindy Kiro]] is sworn in as the 22nd [[Governor-General of New Zealand]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/453964/dame-cindy-kiro-sworn-in-as-governor-general (RNZ)]
